payload.selection_rationale: The single practice proposal fits what the survey measured. The defect is two pinned literals in one PowerShell file (tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1:205 '28 settled', :268 '29 settled'). The tree has moved to 32 and 33, and C-001 and C-003 are already red. The fix is one derived expectation from an oracle the file already uses (Case-C007 compares twinned + settled with Fitness's rule count, RuleCases.ps1:560-567). It leaves eng/rules-parity.ps1 and its three-reader summary format untouched, and everything is cheap to reverse. It also honours the spike's design point: the expected settled count comes from a source independent of the output under test, so C-001 keeps its bite. The practice designer's over_engineering_flag is treated as a real signal, so no scrubber or approved-file tooling, no auto-update switch and no gate wiring (O-005 stays a separate process concern). Three changes were made against reality. (1) The probe runs on a scratch copy of the working tree, not a worktree of HEAD, because the change is uncommitted at build time and a HEAD worktree would run the old pinned RuleCases. (2) The oracle is evaluated lazily inside the cases that use it, not at script scope, so an oracle failure cannot turn every unrelated case red or break a lone -Case run. (3) One architecture rule is added, forbidding a literal settled count in RuleCases.ps1. Nothing runs RuleCases (O-005), but the fitness rules are a gate that does run, so re-pinning becomes a failure somebody sees. No project-scope stack choice was needed: PowerShell for tests/rules and eng/rules-parity.ps1 is already declared.

components.name: Fitness rule-count source (shared with C-007)
components.responsibility: Returns Fitness's rule count exactly the way Case-C007 obtains it today (RuleCases.ps1:560-567). If that expression is inline in C-007 it is lifted into one function that C-007 then calls unchanged. If it is already a function, it is reused as is. It never reads rules-parity output or shares its parser, so the oracle stays independent of the tool under test.
components.key_interactions: Called by ExpectedSettled and by Case-C007. C-007's behaviour and its twinned + settled = rule count assertion do not change.

components.name: ExpectedSettled oracle (lazy, memoised)
components.responsibility: Returns [int] rule count minus the literal 15 twinned that the AGREE line pins. It is computed on first use inside a case and cached for the rest of the run, not at script scope. It throws a named error ('ExpectedSettled: fitness rule count unavailable' or 'ExpectedSettled: derived count <n> < 1') so a broken oracle fails only the cases that use it (C-001, C-003), with a readable message. It must work under Windows PowerShell 5.1 and pwsh 7, so it casts explicitly and wraps in @() where 5.1 returns scalars.
components.key_interactions: Consumed by C-001 and C-003 only. The rule count is read from the real tree, never from C-003's scratch copy, so C-003's +1 stays a real assertion.

components.name: C-001 expected summary line
components.responsibility: Replaces the literal at :205 with 'rules-parity: AGREE 11 facts <- 15 twinned entries, 27 patterns; <ExpectedSettled> settled entries not compared', built by interpolation or concatenation. It keeps the existing CheckRun full-line substring match for every variant: powershell.exe and pwsh, with and without -ExpectFacts 11. It removes the hand-kept per-slice tally comment at :203-204 and replaces it with one line naming where the number comes from. No number appears in code or comments.
components.key_interactions: Checks the summary format printed at eng/rules-parity.ps1:633, which is not changed. Facts, twinned and patterns stay literal on purpose.

components.name: C-003 expected count
components.responsibility: Replaces the literal '29 settled' at :268 with ExpectedSettled + 1: the real tree's derived count plus the one entry C-003 appends below the marker in its scratch copy. Same pin, same red, same one-line cure, so it is done in the same change.
components.key_interactions: Uses the same helper. If the oracle were computed after the append, the +1 would be tautological, so it is computed from the unmodified tree.

components.name: No-literal-settled-count guard rule
components.responsibility: One architecture rule (below) that fails the fitness gate if a literal '<digits> settled entr(y|ies)' is written back into RuleCases.ps1. The engine appends it to .taad/fitness.yaml as a settled entry when the design is accepted. It is not hand-edited.
components.key_interactions: Adding it grows the settled count by the very mechanism this slice fixes, so the build sees a tree one entry larger than the survey's 32. This is a free live check that the derived C-001 survives growth.

components.name: Growth-and-bite probe (throwaway, not committed)
components.responsibility: A build-time check on a scratch copy of the working tree in $env:TEMP, overlaying the modified RuleCases.ps1. It is not a worktree of HEAD, because the change is uncommitted. (a) Append one, then two, settled entries under a single marker: C-001 must exit 0. (b) Make the tool print settled+1: C-001 must exit 1. (c) Make the tool print a non-AGREE verdict: exit 1. (d) Make it classify one twinned entry as settled (14 twinned, settled+1): exit 1. If .taad/fitness.yaml is not tracked, the scratch copy is a plain copy, and the real file is never appended to. Exit codes are read from $LASTEXITCODE straight after each call, never through a pipe.
components.key_interactions: Reuses C-003's 'entry appended below the marker' template. It touches nothing in the repo and is deleted afterwards.

key_decisions.decision: The expected settled count is Fitness's rule count minus the pinned twinned count (15). It is never read back from the parity output under test, and never derived by counting '# settled by SL-' markers.
key_decisions.rationale: Reading it from the tool makes C-001 assert itself, which the spike warned against. Markers are per slice, not per entry (3 markers for 4 new entries between 28 and 32), so a marker count would be wrong. Rule count minus twinned is independent: if the tool drops a settled entry the tool says N-1 and the oracle says N; if it misclassifies a twinned entry the pinned '15 twinned' fails. The slice note's '7' is stale (28 in the file, 32 in the tree), so no number goes into code or comments.

key_decisions.decision: Keep the exact full-line substring match through CheckRun and fill in only the settled number. Do not use a `\d+` wildcard.
key_decisions.rationale: A wildcard is the expect.any(Number) failure: it passes whatever the value is. One interpolated number keeps AGREE, 11, 15, 27 and the wording exactly checked.

key_decisions.decision: Facts (11), twinned (15) and patterns (27) stay literal.
key_decisions.rationale: They did not move while settled went 28 to 32 across SL-044, SL-046 and SL-047. A change to them means someone deliberately edited the parity tool, and a hand edit to the case is the right cost for that.

key_decisions.decision: Fix C-003 in the same change with ExpectedSettled + 1.
key_decisions.rationale: Measured red (29 expected, 33 seen) with the identical flaw. Leaving it keeps the suite red after this slice, which is the harm the slice exists to remove. It is the same file, the same helper and one line.

key_decisions.decision: The oracle is lazy and memoised, evaluated inside C-001, C-003 and C-007, not at script scope. Its rule-count source is the one C-007 already uses, lifted into a shared function if inline.
key_decisions.rationale: Changed from the proposal, which computed it once at script scope. That would turn any oracle failure (for example the interpreter or fitness source missing) into a whole-suite failure, including for a lone -Case run of an unrelated case. Lazy evaluation confines the failure to the cases that need the number. It also lets the cases run alone.

key_decisions.decision: Prove growth and bite with a throwaway probe on a scratch copy of the working tree with the modified RuleCases.ps1 overlaid, not a worktree of HEAD. It has no permanent fixture in the suite.
key_decisions.rationale: Changed from the proposal. The change is uncommitted at build time, so a HEAD worktree runs the old pinned RuleCases and proves nothing. Criteria 2 and 3 are claims about future and broken trees, and a one-off mutation shows both without adding machinery to a suite no gate runs. C-003 already builds a scratch copy, so the approach has precedent.

key_decisions.decision: Declare one architecture rule: RuleCases.ps1 must not contain a literal '<digits> settled entr(y|ies)'.
key_decisions.rationale: The defect has recurred (SL-043 hand refresh, SL-044 drift, now 28 vs 32) precisely because no gate runs RuleCases (O-005). The fitness gate does run, so it can fail where the suite cannot. The pattern matches only the literal summary text. It matches both pre-fix lines (:205, :268) and, by construction, no interpolated form such as '$n settled' or C-007's '(\d+) settled'.

key_decisions.decision: Do not wire RuleCases.ps1 into any engine gate. O-005 stays open.
key_decisions.rationale: A gate changes an engine stage contract and is a process slice of its own. This slice removes the drift that keeps the suite red and adds the one rule that stops it coming back.

key_decisions.decision: C-007 must be run green on the current tree before the oracle is trusted.
key_decisions.rationale: The oracle's arithmetic is C-007's twinned + settled = rule count. The build-check read C-007 (RuleCases.ps1:560-567) but did not run it. If it is red, the design does not hold and the slice goes back to build-check.

contracts.name: ExpectedSettled (script-scope function in tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1)
contracts.notes: Takes no input and returns [int] >= 1. It is lazy and memoised per run, and reads the real tree via the same source as Case-C007. It never reads eng/rules-parity.ps1 output.
contracts.error_cases: Throws 'ExpectedSettled: fitness rule count unavailable' when the C-007 source yields nothing or a non-integer. Throws 'ExpectedSettled: derived count <n> < 1' when rule count minus 15 is not positive. Either way only the calling case fails, with that message.

contracts.name: RuleCases.ps1 -Case C-001 | C-003 | C-007
contracts.notes: The interface is unchanged. It exits 0 on the current tree and stays 0 after any slice appends settled entries, including this slice's own guard rule. It exits 1 when the parity summary's settled count differs from rule count minus 15, when any literal part (verdict, 11, 15, 27, wording) differs, or when the verdict is not AGREE. Run under both powershell.exe and pwsh.
contracts.error_cases: If C-007 is red on the current tree the oracle is invalid: stop and return the slice to build-check.

contracts.name: rules-parity summary line (eng/rules-parity.ps1:633)
contracts.notes: Unchanged. It has three readers in RuleCases (C-001, C-003, C-007), so changing its format would be an expensive contract change. This slice deliberately avoids it.

architecture_rules.name: the rule-case suite never pins a literal settled-entry count
architecture_rules.because: Every slice that declares architecture_rules appends settled entries, so a pinned count goes stale on the next one. It went 28 to 32 with C-001 and C-003 already red, and SL-043 refreshed it by hand. No gate runs RuleCases (O-005), so this fitness rule is the only place a re-pin can fail visibly. The expected count must come from the Fitness rule count minus the twinned count.

cases.behaviour: C-001 asserts the parity summary line (both shells, with and without -ExpectFacts 11)
cases.shape: the current tree, which by build time already includes this slice's own appended guard-rule entry, so the settled count is larger than the survey's 32
cases.why: Proves the derived expectation matches the tool on a tree bigger than any number written in the design. Any pinned or stale figure fails here first.

cases.behaviour: C-001 stays green as later slices append settled entries
cases.shape: scratch copy of the working tree with one extra settled entry appended below the marker
cases.why: This is the slice's defect: the count grows and the suite must not go red. The oracle and the tool must both follow the tree.

cases.behaviour: C-001 stays green as later slices append settled entries
cases.shape: a single slice appends two settled entries under one '# settled by' marker
cases.why: Measured: 3 markers covered 4 new entries between 28 and 32. A marker-counting oracle passes the one-entry probe and fails here, so only a rule-count oracle passes.

cases.behaviour: C-001 still fails when the count is wrong
cases.shape: the parity tool prints settled+1 (scratch copy with eng/rules-parity.ps1:633 mutated)
cases.why: Keeps the check from being tautological. If the expected value were read from the tool's own output, this would still pass.

cases.behaviour: C-001 still fails when parity is not AGREE
cases.shape: the tool prints a non-AGREE verdict with otherwise identical counts
cases.why: Criterion 3. The full-line substring must still reject a wrong verdict after the settled number is interpolated.

cases.behaviour: C-001 does not let the oracle absorb a misclassification
cases.shape: the tool classes one twinned entry as settled (14 twinned, settled+1)
cases.why: The oracle subtracts the pinned 15, not the tool's twinned figure. If it used the tool's twinned figure this shape would pass wrongly. The pinned '15 twinned' must fail it.

cases.behaviour: C-003 asserts the count after appending an entry below the marker
cases.shape: the scratch copy holds one more entry than the real tree, and the base is taken from the unmodified real tree
cases.why: If the base were computed from the scratch copy, +1 would be self-satisfying and C-003 could not fail. It must fail if the tool does not move by exactly one.

cases.shape: the source is unavailable (interpreter or fitness data missing), or C-001 is run alone with -Case C-001
cases.why: The oracle may pick up a dependency C-007 already has. It must fail with the named ExpectedSettled message, and only for the cases that use it. An unrelated -Case must be unaffected because evaluation is lazy.

cases.shape: powershell.exe 5.1 versus pwsh 7 returning a scalar, a single object or an array for the rule count
cases.why: 5.1 and 7 differ in scalar and array unrolling and in .Count on a single object. An unforced cast would yield a wrong or odd expected string in one shell only.

cases.shape: C-007 (twinned + settled = Fitness rule count) run on the current tree
cases.why: The oracle's arithmetic is exactly that equation. C-007 was read but never run, and if it is red the design does not hold.

cases.behaviour: guard rule fires on the defect and not on correct code
cases.shape: the pre-fix RuleCases.ps1 (literals at :205 and :268) versus the post-fix file
cases.why: A rule that matches nothing can never fail, and one that matches correct code gets deleted. The pattern must hit both pre-fix lines, and must not hit the interpolated form or C-007's '(\d+) settled' regex.

cases.behaviour: oracle guard for a non-positive derived count
cases.why: Unreachable while the tree holds at least 15 twinned and many settled entries, and testing it needs a synthetic fitness file wired into the oracle. The guard is a one-line throw, and if it were ever hit the resulting mismatch would still be loud.

proposals.note: The only proposal, and its core (derive settled from Fitness's rule count minus the pinned twinned count, keep the full-line substring, fix C-003 alongside) was selected whole. Three changes were made: the probe overlays the working tree instead of using a HEAD worktree, the oracle is lazy rather than script-scope, and one guard rule was added.

payload.coherence_check: One proposal, no composition to check. Nobody has disagreed with this design, and that is the first thing for the reviewer to argue with. Instead of checking two proposals against each other, the proposal was checked against what the survey measured and against itself. (1) Its premise that appending slices move only settled is measured: settled went 28 to 32 with 11 facts, 15 twinned and 27 patterns constant, so the literal 11/15/27 plus a derived settled is coherent. (2) The oracle's independence is the load-bearing invariant. Case-C007 pairs a PowerShell parse of the parity output with Fitness's rule count, which suggests two implementations. That is read, not run, so it is a must-verify: run C-007 green and read :560-567 before trusting it. If it fails, the oracle source changes, hence the decidable disagreement below. (3) A seam the proposal missed was corrected: its probe used a worktree of HEAD, which lacks the uncommitted change. The probe now overlays the working tree. (4) Script-scope evaluation of the oracle would have coupled an oracle failure to every case, so it was made lazy. (5) A seam the design creates itself: declaring the guard rule makes the engine append a settled entry at design acceptance, so the build sees a tree larger than the surveyed 32. This is the very growth the fix must survive, and the engine must append it as settled (below the marker). If it landed as a compared pattern, 27 would move and C-001 would go red on the literals, so the build checks patterns is still 27 after acceptance. (6) The slice note's '7 settled' is stale against the measured 28 in the file and 32 in the tree. The measurement outranks the note, and no count belongs in code or comments. (7) Architecture rules: exactly one, on the literal count, because that is the only seam whose crossing is a real defect and is expressible as a line-scoped pattern. The oracle-independence property (must not read parity output) is not expressible without a multi-line match, so it is held by a case and by review, not by a rule. The design constrains nothing about who may depend on whom, so there is no must_not_import rule.

decidable_disagreements.question: Is Fitness's rule count, as Case-C007 obtains it, an independent oracle that C-001 and C-003 can also obtain (including on a lone -Case run), and does C-007 pass on the current tree?
decidable_disagreements.positions: The proposal assumes yes from reading RuleCases.ps1:560-567 without running C-007. If no (the count comes from parity output or a shared parser, needs an interpreter parameter the lone cases lack, or twinned + settled != rule count), the oracle source has to be replaced by a direct per-entry count of .taad/fitness.yaml (not per marker), or the slice returns to build-check.

taste_disagreements: Throwaway build-time probe versus a permanent negative test of C-001's bite: a permanent test survives but adds fixture machinery to a suite no gate runs.
Lifting C-007's inline rule-count expression into a shared function versus duplicating it: sharing is one source but touches a green case.

Adding an architecture rule for a one-file test-bookkeeping fix versus relying on the derived count alone: the rule is the only enforcement anyone will see, given O-005, but it adds one more settled entry.
Keeping 11, 15 and 27 as literals versus deriving all four numbers: literals cost a deliberate hand edit only when the parity tool itself changes.
Names and placement of ExpectedSettled and the rule-count function within RuleCases.ps1.
whats_new: Lazy, memoised ExpectedSettled oracle in tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1: Fitness rule count minus the pinned 15 twinned
C-001's expected AGREE line built with the derived count instead of the literal at :205
C-003's expected count set to ExpectedSettled + 1 instead of the literal at :268
The hand-kept per-slice tally comment at :203-204 replaced by a one-line pointer to where the count comes from
One architecture rule (no literal settled-entry count in RuleCases.ps1), enforced by the fitness gate that does run
A throwaway build-time growth-and-bite probe on a scratch copy of the working tree (append one and two entries, mutate the count, mutate the verdict, misclassify a twinned entry)
whats_reused: CheckRun's full-line substring match in C-001, unchanged
Case-C007's Fitness rule-count source (RuleCases.ps1:560-567), reused rather than re-implemented
C-003's scratch-copy and 'entry appended below the marker' template, reused as the probe's appended entry
The existing dual-shell (powershell.exe and pwsh) and with/without -ExpectFacts 11 C-001 variants, all fed by the one helper
eng/rules-parity.ps1 and its summary format at :633, untouched
The engine's own append of declared rules into .taad/fitness.yaml as settled entries

prior_art.pattern: 'Derived Value' instead of 'Hard-Coded Test Data': compute the expected result from the test's inputs so it follows them without a hand refresh. This is what SL-043 did by hand and the pin forces every appending slice to repeat.
A tautological test takes its expected value from the code under test and can never fail. The fix is an independent oracle for the expected value.

Scrubbers in approved snapshots replace volatile values so the golden file stays stable. The known failure is scrubbing a value that mattered, which is why a derived value is used rather than a placeholder.
Snapshot property matchers such as expect.any(Number) stabilise a volatile field but accept any value of that type. This is the failure a bare `\d+` in C-001 would copy.

cross_domain_transfer.source_domain: Snapshot and approval testing (Verify, ApprovalTests, Jest snapshots)
cross_domain_transfer.pattern: Keep an otherwise exact golden line, scrub the one volatile field, and assert that field against an independent oracle rather than a wildcard.
cross_domain_transfer.rationale: C-001 is an approval test of one golden line whose only moving field is the settled count. The analogy is real but thin: it amounts to the derived-value pattern already in xUnit practice, and the design does not depend on it. What it contributes is the warning about the two failure modes, re-approving by reflex (SL-043's hand refresh) and a toothless wildcard.

invariants.precondition: There is an independent source for the settled count that does not share rules-parity.ps1's classification: Fitness's rule count, with twinned + settled = rule count.
invariants.evidence: The build-check read Case-C007 (RuleCases.ps1:560-567) comparing twinned + settled with Fitness's rule count but did not run it. Check: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1 -Case C-007, then $LASTEXITCODE is 0.

invariants.precondition: Slices that append architecture_rules change only the settled count, not facts, twinned or patterns.
invariants.evidence: Measured: settled went 28 to 32 across SL-044, SL-046 and SL-047 while parity still printed '11 facts <- 15 twinned entries, 27 patterns'.

invariants.precondition: C-001 and C-003 are the only places that pin a settled count.
invariants.evidence: The build-check grepped tests/ and eng/ for '\d+ settled' and 'entries not compared' and found only RuleCases.ps1:205 and :268.

invariants.precondition: The Fitness rule-count source runs under both Windows PowerShell 5.1 and pwsh 7, and can be obtained when C-001 or C-003 is run alone.
invariants.evidence: Not measured. Settled by running C-001, C-003 and C-007 under powershell.exe and pwsh after the change, including a lone -Case run.

invariants.precondition: This slice's own guard-rule entry is appended by the engine as a settled entry and leaves facts, twinned and patterns unchanged.
invariants.evidence: Inferred from SL-044, SL-046 and SL-047 behaving that way. Check by running eng/rules-parity.ps1 after design acceptance and confirming '11 facts <- 15 twinned entries, 27 patterns'.
